question: A 72-year-old man comes to the physician because of several episodes of dark urine over the past 2 months. He has had a 6 kg (13.2-lb) weight loss over the past 3 months despite no changes in appetite. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. A CT scan shows a heterogeneous enhancing mass arising from the left renal pelvis. Pathologic examination of the lesion is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Ulcerating tumor comprised of glandular cells within mucinous material
options.opb: Pedunculated tumor comprised of pleomorphic urothelial cells with severe nuclear atypia
options.opc: Tumor with central scar comprised of large eosinophilic cells with central nuclei
options.opd: Bright yellow tumor comprised of polygonal cells filled with lipids and glycogen
options.ope: Grayish-tan tumor comprised of primitive blastemal cells forming abortive glomeruli

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "dark urine" -> "weight loss" -> "smoking history" -> "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "likely urothelial carcinoma" -> "pleomorphic urothelial cells with severe nuclear atypia" -> 85%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "dark urine" -> "weight loss" -> "smoking history" -> "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "possible renal cell carcinoma" -> "polygonal cells filled with lipids and glycogen" -> 60%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "dark urine" -> "weight loss" -> "smoking history" -> "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "less likely Wilms tumor" -> "primitive blastemal cells forming abortive glomeruli" -> 40%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "dark urine" -> "weight loss" -> "smoking history" -> "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "unlikely oncocytoma" -> "large eosinophilic cells with central nuclei" -> 30%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "dark urine" -> "weight loss" -> "smoking history" -> "CT scan shows mass in renal pelvis" -> "unlikely mucinous adenocarcinoma" -> "glandular cells within mucinous material" -> 25%
analysis: The clinical presentation and CT findings suggest a renal pelvis tumor, likely a urothelial carcinoma. The patient's history of smoking is a significant risk factor for urothelial carcinoma. Pathologically, urothelial carcinoma is characterized by pleomorphic urothelial cells with nuclear atypia, often forming papillary structures. Therefore, the most likely pathological finding in this case is a pedunculated tumor comprised of pleomorphic urothelial cells with severe nuclear atypia.
